tools.name: get_asset_state
tools.description: Return an asset's static properties and its observed/derived metrics for a given year. Use this to understand what the asset is and how it is performing.

tools.name: get_asset_evidence
tools.description: Return the human-readable evidence lines that the deadspace engine produced for this asset.

tools.name: get_deadspace_status
tools.description: Return the B6 status, flags, urgency, and contributing factors for an asset.

tools.name: get_catchment_profile
tools.description: Return the walking or driving catchment profile: per-threshold population and coverage ratios.

tools.name: get_population_profile
tools.description: Return the age structure of the population accessible from the asset.

tools.name: get_nearby_assets
tools.description: Return assets within a radius of the given asset.

tools.name: get_available_subtypes
tools.description: Return the taxonomy subtypes for a given asset class. You MUST pick from this list when proposing a repurpose.

tools.name: get_development_candidates
tools.description: Return candidate development options for a parcel.

tools.name: get_taxonomy_entry
tools.description: Return the full taxonomy definition for a subtype.

tools.name: get_assumptions_slice
tools.description: Return specific top-level sections of the model assumptions (e.g. huff, accessibility, occupancy_dynamics).

tools.name: get_interventions_history
tools.description: Return interventions that have targeted this asset across any scenario.

tools.name: get_action_space
tools.description: Return the intervention types applicable to a given asset type.

tools.name: get_lease_schedule
tools.description: Return the commercial asset's lease schedule: total leases, next expiry year, anchor lease details, and a per-year expiry calendar. Use this to time a structural intervention (repurpose, retrofit that closes the asset) for after anchor lease expiry.

tools.name: get_asset_trajectory
tools.description: Return the asset's five-year trajectory classification and supporting features (peak occupancy, years since peak, occupancy trend). Use this to distinguish a stable low from a rapid decline from a recovery.
